note: The browser rows are measured on the nightly runner (ubuntu-24.04-arm, headless Chromium, seed 7, 60 s a row), from the audio-quality-run artifacts of the seven scheduled Nightly runs on main from 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-04 (40885347517, 41065371094, 41204380716, 41313466339, 41483654426, 41656613559, 41852517544), the first after a fresh subscriber stopped receiving the relay's cached history. The AAC rows predate the TS importer publishing each PES as one group. Each ceiling is the worst of its seven nights times 1.25, plus one runner hiccup, rounded up to two significant figures. The hiccup is sized from the single gaps the 2026-10-08 night put on otherwise clean rows, the fixed-250 control among them: 250 underruns/min, 700 gap ms/min, 3.3 skips/min, 280 discarded ms/min, 0.01 stalled, 0.015 silence, and one 20 ms bucket of target. Budgeted this way, every night passes when it is held out of its row's measurement except one, and that row's own ceiling includes it: the 2026-11-03 Opus bursty row raised its target to 300 ms 2.6 s in and held it for one 20 s half-life before settling at 180. Such startup holds, Opus near-zero's 100 ms on 2026-10-30 and 10-31 among them, are budgeted as measured. These ceilings record today's player as the runner hears it, not target audio quality. To re-measure, download the same artifact from the latest scheduled nightlies (`gh run download <id> -n audio-quality-run`), which keep every run, and apply the same rule. The replay rows are deterministic, so their ceilings are exactly what they measured, through the end of each recording, with no headroom: any regression fails them, and an improvement should be tightened in. They were last re-measured on 2026-10-22 using version 3 traces with encoded frame durations: AAC-LC uses its fixed 1024 samples, and relay-mic retains Opus packet TOC durations. relay-mic was re-recorded on 2026-11-03 from a real microphone, Chrome 156 on a MacBook Air publishing its built-in microphone through the public relay, recorded by headless Chromium on a Linux host (35 s, minimum RTT 2 ms), which raised its target ceiling from 60 to 80 ms and its silence from 0 to 0.001 as measured. The recording path itself has no added RTT. relay-mic-rtt40 is the 2026-11-03 Chrome row at 40 ms of added RTT on that laptop (180 s, minimum RTT 47 ms), kept as the baseline time stretch improves on; like every replay row, its player_underruns_per_min ceiling is what it measures, not a fixed zero. player_underruns_per_min, the player's own counter that its stats panel shows, is budgeted on the replay rows only; it counts the run-dry re-stalls the tap files as stalled time. On 2026-11-07, after the ordered read stopped delivering groups below its cursor (#8071) and took Rust's hole and age bounds (#8218), relay-bbb was re-measured at 16.1 player underruns/min, 0.025 stalled and 0.02 silence, and relay-mic-rtt40 at 8.2, its discarded audio at 70.9 ms/min and its target p95 at 320 ms rather than 780, since the stale backlog it never played no longer reaches the estimator; neither row lost audio the previous player heard. On 2026-11-08 the player began time-stretching live playback with NetEq's accelerate, deciding on the ring's depth right after each arrival and never expanding, and every replay row was re-measured with it, the browser rows left to the nightly runner. Each row's av_lag_ms ceilings, how far the playhead trails the shared clock video plays from, are what it measured: the ring rests one frame ahead of the newest arrival's playout, as the trim it replaces left it, so audio leads the clock by 19 to 23 ms at p50, and any change that settles audio later to buy fewer underruns fails them. Against the trim, the A/V lag p50 fell from 0.7, -17.5, -21.5, -18.2 and -15.6 ms to -22.4 on bursty-aac, -22.2 on local-aac, -22.7 on relay-bbb, -19 on relay-mic and -20.1 on relay-mic-rtt40, and its p95 fell on every row, most on relay-bbb (10.5 to -4.2) and relay-mic-rtt40 (-0.9 to -13.4). Underruns stayed where the trim had them, as the latency they would cost is not spent: player_underruns_per_min held at 4.4, 12.1, 16.1 and 6.1 and rose from 8.2 to 10.6 on relay-mic-rtt40, and relay-mic's tap now files 2 short quanta a minute, 2 ms of missing audio, where it filed none. What the stretch buys is the audio the trim dropped: discarded_ms_per_min fell from 87.8 to 0 on relay-bbb and from 127.5 to 100.6 on local-aac, whose remainder drops nothing: two receive stalls 14 and 15.3 s in leave audio 159 and 132 ms behind the clock, and the fast accelerate that brings it back within half a second steps the playhead's lag the way skip_aheads reads as a skip. player_skips_per_min, the ring's own count of re-anchors that dropped buffered audio, is budgeted beside it, at 0 on every row. Once durations became whole nanoseconds, relay-bbb's delay, 200 ms plus one 1024-sample AAC frame, rounds up by a fraction of a sample, so its ring holds one more sample (23 µs) and its A/V lag p50 measures -22.6 rather than -22.7. Neither replay calibration changed the browser or native ceilings. bursty-aac is the 2026-10-18 AAC bursty isolated capture, recorded with the observer subscribed at the decoder's 2 s budget, so it holds every group the player saw. The native rows are provisional: measured on a loaded developer host (x86_64 Linux, the private PulseAudio null sink, seed 7, 60 s a row) on 2026-10-17, three runs of every row from the debug build nightly uses plus three more of the AAC rows from a release build, which played alike. Each ceiling is the worst clean run times 1.25, plus one native hiccup sized from the unimpaired Opus row's worst run (20 underruns/min, 50 gap ms/min, 2.2 skips/min, 110 discarded ms/min, 0.01 stalled, 0.005 silence, one 20 ms bucket of target), rounded up to two significant figures. On that host the null sink's clock ran about 150 ppm slow against the monotonic clock, read within 5 ms at p95 per sample, and its output latency sat between 14 and 28 ms. Five of the 36 AAC rows (none of the 18 Opus rows) voided on the clock: the device stopped pulling for about two seconds mid-row, sometimes after a backend error and a stream restart, which is a native playback defect rather than noise, and the ceilings exclude those runs. Re-measure from the nightly runner's artifacts once it has a week of native rows.
